name: Thijs Reuten - § 28 - Am 11
title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 28. Regrets the weakening of non-proliferation, disarmament and arms control regimes; calls for the redoubling of efforts to reverse this trend and demands that the EU play a much stronger role, in particular in the field of non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; calls, in this regard, for the EU to actively support the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and to work towards its implementation and further ratification by the EU Member States that have not done so; reaffirms its full support for the EU and its Member States’ commitment to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons as the cornerstone of the nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament regime; stresses the need for greater transparency and convergence at national and EU level on arms exports, especially during a period of increased defence spending and EDTIB; calls on the Member States to respect the EU Common Position on Arms Exports; calls on the Member States to fully comply with Common Position 2008/944/CFSP and to strictly implement Criterion Four on regional stability and halt arms export licensing if there is a clear risk that the intended recipient might use the arms aggressively against another country in general and the Member States in particular; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 10 Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP of 8 December 2008 defining common rules governing control of exports of military technology and equipment, (OJ L 335, 13.12.2008, p. 99, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/compos/2008/944/oj).
